evidence_catalog.claim: For model/shuffle seeds 44/43, the recorded configurations differ only in learning rate (0.05 versus 0.1).
For model/shuffle seeds 44/43, the largest one-epoch validation-loss rise was none at learning rate 0.05 and +0.5489 (epochs 1→2) at 0.1.
For model/shuffle seeds 44/43, final validation accuracy was 75.15% at learning rate 0.05 and 71.25% at 0.1 (-3.90 percentage points for high minus low).
For model/shuffle seeds 144/143, the recorded configurations differ only in learning rate (0.05 versus 0.1).
For model/shuffle seeds 144/143, the largest one-epoch validation-loss rise was +0.0012 (epochs 3→4) at learning rate 0.05 and +0.1005 (epochs 3→4) at 0.1.
For model/shuffle seeds 144/143, final validation accuracy was 76.05% at learning rate 0.05 and 76.35% at 0.1 (+0.30 percentage points for high minus low).
For model/shuffle seeds 244/243, the recorded configurations differ only in learning rate (0.05 versus 0.1).
For model/shuffle seeds 244/243, the largest one-epoch validation-loss rise was none at learning rate 0.05 and +0.1387 (epochs 1→2) at 0.1.
For model/shuffle seeds 244/243, final validation accuracy was 75.90% at learning rate 0.05 and 71.45% at 0.1 (-4.45 percentage points for high minus low).
Across 3 matched seed blocks, the high-minus-low final validation-accuracy differences were -3.90, +0.30, -4.45 percentage points in listed order; the direction varied.

loss_rise.description: The higher learning rate may be associated with larger temporary validation-loss rises in this setup.
loss_rise.missing_evidence: More matched seed blocks and finer training measurements would show whether this pattern persists and help investigate the training trajectory.

accuracy_drop.description: The higher learning rate may reduce final validation accuracy across seed blocks.
accuracy_drop.missing_evidence: More matched seed blocks on the same validation split would show how often the final-accuracy difference is negative.

seed_dependence.description: The final-accuracy effect of learning rate may depend on the model and shuffle seeds.
seed_dependence.missing_evidence: More matched seed blocks, each with both learning rates and the same validation split, would show how often the final-accuracy difference changes direction.
